title: A World Model of Radiologist Reading for Medical Image Representation Learning
domain: Chest radiography; radiologist visual-search representation learning
dataset_or_cohort: MIMIC-EYE/MIMIC-CXR for pretraining; GazeSearch ChestSearch; CheXpert; RSNA Pneumonia; SIIM-ACR Pneumothorax
sample_scale: MIMIC-EYE: 3,032 frontal CXRs; GazeSearch: 3,870 train and 488 test images; external diagnosis datasets: CheXpert 224,316 images, RSNA 26,684, SIIM-ACR 12,047
institution_count: MIMIC-EYE derives from one hospital; external datasets add distinct sources, exact aggregate institution count NI
split_strategy: Official MIMIC-EYE split 2,729/151/152; GazeSearch 3,870/488; downstream benchmark splits and fixed-seed label fractions
observation_process: Static frontal CXR paired with temporally ordered 60-Hz gaze and dwell time; fixations mapped to image patches and repeated visits merged
state: Image-patch latents plus the prefix of gaze-ordered visited patches with spatial, temporal, and dwell embeddings
observation_decoder: Predicts the next fixated-patch latent and spatially completes unvisited patches; frozen representations feed diagnosis and seven-fixation scanpath heads
action: Radiologist fixation sequence/order; no clinical treatment or robot-control action
transition_mechanism: JEPA-style causal Transformer predicts next-fixation latent against an EMA target encoder; cross-attention performs spatial completion
maximum_horizon: One fixation step during pretraining; downstream scanpath decoder emits seven fixations
rollout_regime: Teacher-forced observed gaze prefixes during pretraining; downstream inference starts from the image and does not freely simulate clinical state
capability_claim: Passive behavioral forecasting and representation learning, not intervention simulation
baselines: BioViL, MedKLIP, MGCA, GLoRIA, PRIOR, MedCLIP, CheXWorld, EGMA; GazeFormer, HAT, GazeSearch, LogitGaze variants
state_fidelity_metrics: Diagnosis AUROC, accuracy, and F1; scanpath ScanMatch, SED, STDE, and MultiMatch; no direct latent-state fidelity metric
transition_metrics: Next-fixation/scanpath metrics and downstream transfer; no clinical transition outcome metric
action_sensitivity: Chronological versus raster/random order; autoregressive-only and spatial-completion-only ablations
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI; no calibration or predictive-uncertainty evaluation
external_validation: Transfer evaluated on CheXpert, RSNA, SIIM-ACR, and GazeSearch, but not in prospective clinical deployment
decision_utility: Frozen-feature diagnosis and scanpath probing only; no decision-impact study
statistical_analysis: Fixed-seed label fractions; no confidence intervals or repeated-run variance reported
causal_language: Uses causal attention/order terminology only; no causal treatment-effect claim
estimand: Prediction of expert gaze and image labels under the observed data distribution
data_access: MIMIC data require credentialed access; other benchmark access varies by dataset
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed gaze-to-patch conversion, architecture, training, and downstream protocols
randomness: Fixed seed reported for label-fraction sampling; multi-seed model evaluation NI
evidence_anchors: Abstract p.1; Sec. 3 and Fig. 1 pp.3-5; Sec. 4 and Tables 1-5 pp.5-9; Limitations p.10; Appendices A-B pp.13-15
appraisal_strengths: Controlled objective and ordering ablations; several external image benchmarks; explicit visual-search metrics
appraisal_limitations: One gaze corpus and chest-radiography setting; no free-running dynamics, calibration, or statistical uncertainty; some baseline backbones differ

title: Arti-JEPA: Adapting Video World Model to Real-Time MRI of the Vocal Tract for Speech-Production Analysis
domain: Real-time MRI of the vocal tract; speech-production representation learning
dataset_or_cohort: USC 75-speaker rtMRI corpus; in-house longitudinal rtMRI; Annot-16, USC LSS, GLOSS glossectomy, and stuttering evaluation cohorts
sample_scale: Pretraining: 92 speakers, 9,353 videos, 61.9 hours, 20.1M frames; evaluation includes Annot-16 16 speakers, USC LSS one speaker, GLOSS three individuals, and stuttering seven adults
institution_count: USC plus in-house and clinical cohorts; exact collection-site count NI
split_strategy: Subject-disjoint and scanner-aware splits; phoneme probe uses 14 Annot-16 training speakers, one validation speaker, one test speaker, and USC LSS OOD; stuttering uses leave-one-subject-out
observation_process: Grayscale rtMRI at 61-99 fps resampled to 50 fps; 32-frame, 0.64-second clips; audio and labels withheld from central self-supervision
state: Spatiotemporal V-JEPA2 latent representation of a vocal-tract rtMRI clip
observation_decoder: Masked latent prediction; frozen probes decode phonemes, disfluency, and glossectomy status
action: No action in the central model; audio conditioning is an appendix experiment
action_provenance: NA for central model; observed audio in exploratory appendix experiment
transition_mechanism: Masked latent JEPA within clips after domain adaptation of V-JEPA2
maximum_horizon: 32 frames or 0.64 seconds; exploratory audio-conditioned rollout is within the same window
rollout_regime: Masked self-supervised prediction, not central free-running temporal rollout
capability_claim: Passive dynamics representation learning and measurement, not intervention simulation
baselines: Adapted and stock VideoMAE; stock V-JEPA2; DINOv2; ImageNet ViT; frozen-probe comparisons
state_fidelity_metrics: Cohen kappa, phoneme error rate, macro-F1, balanced accuracy; representation standard deviation, effective rank, and cosine-similarity collapse diagnostics
transition_metrics: Probe performance and masked-prediction representation diagnostics; no patient-state transition metric
rollout_stability: Collapse diagnostics are reported, but no long-horizon rollout-drift evaluation
action_sensitivity: Domain-adaptation, video-versus-image, loss/context ablations; permuted-audio appendix test shows limited use of audio
external_validation: USC LSS is an out-of-distribution scanner/speaker test; small GLOSS and stuttering clinical cohorts
decision_utility: Representation-based speech measurement only; no clinical decision-impact evaluation
statistical_analysis: Main comparisons report mean and SD over three seeds; no confidence intervals
causal_language: No causal-effect language; world-model terminology refers to learned video structure
estimand: Predictive representation quality for speech-production signals
data_access: Mix of public and private/in-house rtMRI cohorts
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed resampling, clip construction, splits, objectives, probes, and hyperparameters; private data limit full reproduction
evidence_anchors: Abstract pp.1-2; Sec. 3 pp.3-5 and Table 9 p.19; Sec. 4 pp.6-9 and Tables 1-4; clinical evaluations pp.10-15 and Tables 5-8; Appendix Tables 12-20 pp.20-25; Limitations p.16
appraisal_strengths: Subject-disjoint OOD testing, diverse probes, repeated seeds, and a reported negative audio-conditioning result
appraisal_limitations: No clinically meaningful trajectory simulator; very small clinical cohorts; private pretraining data; no uncertainty calibration; audio conditioning was ineffective

title: ChronoMedicalWorld: A Medical World Model for Learning Patient Trajectories from Longitudinal Care Data
domain: Longitudinal chronic kidney disease EHR forecasting
sample_scale: 2,232 patients; 15,070 patient-years; dynamic rollout points 4,875 train, 1,020 validation, 1,078 test
observation_process: Irregular clinical follow-up aggregated by calendar year; annual clinical variables, drug exposure, and patient-clinician messages
missingness: Explicit missingness: urine protein 28.2%, blood pressure 40.0%, no communication 33.3%; missingness flags and measurement counts; zero vector for no communication
censoring_or_competing_events: Eligibility requires at least five annual observations and baseline eGFR above 30; loss to follow-up, death, and competing-event handling NI
state: Nine-dimensional annual dynamic state plus static sex/pathology and target-time covariates
observation_decoder: Predicts next annual eGFR and the next latent state
action: Sixty-two binary drug-exposure indicators plus a 256-dimensional annual patient-clinician communication embedding
action_provenance: Observed exposure/administration and observed communications; dose and adherence NI
transition_mechanism: Recurrent GRU latent JEPA with SIGReg and six physiology-aware loss terms
maximum_horizon: Up to eight annual steps in configuration; dynamic-50-percent-history and fixed-three-year rollouts
rollout_regime: Free-running closed-loop prediction with rollout-prefix training that feeds predictions back; first-step anchor and clipping stabilizers
capability_claim: Action-conditioned forecasting with a what-if interface; not a causally identified counterfactual model
baselines: GPT-5.5 structured-prompt baseline; medication and communication ablations
rollout_stability: Free-running rollout is measured and stabilized, but no violation rate or horizon-stratified drift analysis
action_sensitivity: Communication removal, embedding dimension, message intensity/type, and action-channel variants; no action-shuffle or dose-response test
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI; no calibration or predictive-uncertainty evaluation
decision_utility: Hypothetical digital-twin and decision-support use only; no clinician or policy-impact study
safety_evaluation: Physiology priors, jump penalty, and clipping; no clinical-hazard or subgroup-safety evaluation
statistical_analysis: No confidence intervals or repeated-seed variance reported
causal_language: Uses counterfactual intervention and what-if language while explicitly stating it is not a causal estimator
estimand: Observed-policy trajectory prediction under a supplied future action sequence
counterfactual_validation: No factual-versus-counterfactual ground truth; only observed-trajectory prediction and action-channel ablations
preprocessing_reproducibility: Clinical aggregation and architecture are described, but private extraction and text embeddings prevent full reproduction
evidence_anchors: Abstract p.1; Sec. 2.4 pp.3-4, including non-causal qualification; Sec. 3 and Fig. 1 pp.4-6; Sec. 4 and Tables 1-3 pp.6-8; Sec. 5 and Tables 4-5 pp.8-9; Secs. 6.2 and 6.4 p.10
appraisal_strengths: Patient-level split, explicit missingness representation, free-running rollout training, and action-channel ablations
appraisal_limitations: Single-source selected cohort; one weak LLM baseline; no causal adjustment, overlap check, calibration, external validation, or statistical uncertainty; annual actions are coarse

title: EHRWorld: A Patient-Centric Medical World Model for Long-Horizon Clinical Trajectories
sample_scale: 110,513 hospitalization episodes and about 17.5M events; test set 579 episodes with 84,010 inquiry events, 25,798 intervention events, and 1,043 diagnoses
institution_count: One health system, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center
split_strategy: Patient-centric subject-ID separation is stated; 579 test episodes; remaining training split stratified by diagnostic category; validation size NI
observation_process: Irregular timestamped admission-to-discharge event sequences with sets of concurrent events at a timestamp
missingness: Low-activity/incomplete episodes are filtered; imputation and remaining missing-data treatment NI
censoring_or_competing_events: Trajectory ends at discharge; death, discharge type, and competing-event handling NI
state: Timestamp, demographics, diagnoses and rationales, plus complete preceding event history
observation_decoder: Generates explicit values for inquiry events; intervention events are appended to history without an outcome value
action: Medication administrations, procedures, and clinical inquiries
transition_mechanism: Autoregressive LLM conditional set generation followed by deterministic history update
maximum_horizon: Full hospitalization from admission to discharge; fixed maximum event count NI
rollout_regime: Both next-event teacher-forced evaluation and free-running full-trajectory generation
capability_claim: Action-conditioned clinical trajectory simulation; causal and counterfactual wording is not supported by causal identification
baselines: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Pro preview, and multiple open general and medical LLMs; no simple count, repeat, or action-agnostic baseline
state_fidelity_metrics: Clinical-status F1 and event label precision, recall, and F1
transition_metrics: Set similarity at 10/15/25, SMAPE for values, and event-label metrics
rollout_stability: Next-step versus full-trajectory retention rate and a greater-than-50-percent-change stress subset
action_sensitivity: NI; no action removal, shuffle, or perturbation evaluation
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI; no calibration or uncertainty evaluation
external_validation: None; all data derive from MIMIC-IV
decision_utility: No downstream treatment optimization, clinician study, or prospective decision-utility test
safety_evaluation: Ethics section notes observational bias and need for human oversight; no operational safety test
statistical_analysis: No confidence intervals or repeated-seed variance reported
causal_language: Describes causal sequential and causally grounded simulation and mentions counterfactual futures
estimand: Prediction of future events under the observed hospital policy
data_access: MIMIC-IV is credentialed; availability of the derived EHRWorld-110K resource NI
preprocessing_reproducibility: Event extraction, filtering, prompts, and evaluation are described; derived data and code availability remain unclear
evidence_anchors: Abstract pp.1-2; Sec. 3 and Fig. 2 pp.3-4; Sec. 4 pp.4-5 and Algorithm 1 p.13; Sec. 5 pp.5-8, Tables 1-2, and Fig. 3; Limitations and Ethics p.9; Appendices A and C pp.11-14
appraisal_strengths: Full-hospitalization evaluation, explicit next-step versus rollout retention, patient separation, and a high-sensitivity stress test
appraisal_limitations: Causal language exceeds evidence; no confounding or overlap analysis, calibration, action ablation, external validation, simple baselines, or released derived resource

title: GEMEO: the first patient world model for rare disease, grounding generative clinical trajectories in the genome and a biomedical knowledge graph
domain: Rare-disease longitudinal EHR, genomics proposal, and biomedical knowledge graph
dataset_or_cohort: Linked Brazilian SUS national subsystems; GEMEO training cohort and RareBench-BR
sample_scale: 42,265 patients and 2.4M events for world-model training; RareBench-BR 44,051 trajectories; action analysis 12,380 held-out treatment initiators
institution_count: Multiple national administrative and clinical subsystems; exact institution count NI
split_strategy: Patient-level 70/15/15 split; geographically external test is claimed but detailed partitioning NI
observation_process: Sparse irregular MEDS v0.4.1 event stream; at least four events and two codes per patient
censoring_or_competing_events: Competing-risk head uses 4,624 deaths; main trajectory censoring and loss-to-follow-up handling NI
state: Manifest clinical event codes with optional PrimeKG context; genome-conditioned state is proposed, but flagship experiments use structured events without patient genomes
observation_decoder: Predicts next novel clinical-event distribution and variable-horizon sequences; proposer-verifier produces evidence paths
action: Treatment or dispensing event token; flagship version collapses many treatments to unknown, while an action variant retains 65 actions
transition_mechanism: Twenty-million-parameter eight-layer Causal Diffusion Forcing Transformer with recurrence-aware cross-entropy and gated PrimeKG cross-attention
maximum_horizon: Variable, up to context length 512; evaluations include 12-month transitions and discontinuation beyond six months
rollout_regime: Autoregressive/full-sequence diffusion; action test compares actual-treatment versus masked-action prefixes; Level-3 counterfactual rollout not performed
capability_claim: Validated for Level-1 prediction and a Level-2 action-association test; Level-3 counterfactual capability is a design target only
baselines: Frequency, count, bigram, and repeat-last baselines
state_fidelity_metrics: New-onset Top-1, AUROC, recall at 1, genomic AUROC, survival concordance
transition_metrics: Action delta-log-probability and KL divergence; long-context task metrics
rollout_stability: Long-context tasks are evaluated, but no trajectory-drift or clinical-constraint failure metric
action_sensitivity: Actual-treatment versus masked-action prefixes; reported delta-log-probability and KL divergence
calibration_and_uncertainty: Integrated calibration index reported; method detail is limited; 2,000-bootstrap confidence intervals
external_validation: A geographically external test is claimed, but source and partition details are sparse
decision_utility: Research benchmark and proposer-verifier evidence paths; no prospective clinician or decision-impact study
safety_evaluation: Deterministic evidence paths and research-only oversight language; no recommendation-hazard evaluation
causal_language: Uses counterfactual language for a future Level-3 target; current action test is associative
estimand: Future-event likelihood under an observed actual versus masked treatment token, not a treatment effect
counterfactual_validation: None; synthetic-SCM and trial-replication counterfactual validation are future work
data_access: Public benchmark under CC-BY-NC-4.0; underlying linked extraction is not openly redistributable
preprocessing_reproducibility: Pipeline and artifact claims are described, but external reproduction of the underlying extraction is restricted
evidence_anchors: Abstract p.1; Sec. 2 pp.2-3; Sec. 3 pp.3-6 and Tables 1-3; Sec. 4 p.6; Methods p.7; Limitations, Ethics, and Data statements pp.7-8
appraisal_strengths: Explicit capability-level boundary, strong simple baselines, action-mask test, bootstrap intervals, and open code/weights/benchmark
appraisal_limitations: Self-released non-peer-reviewed manuscript; headline combines many components; flagship is not genome-conditioned; no causal or Level-3 counterfactual validation; external-test detail is sparse

title: NeuroWorld: A Latent Brain World Model for Stimulus-Conditioned Human Brain Dynamics
domain: Naturalistic movie fMRI and stimulus-conditioned brain dynamics
dataset_or_cohort: Algonauts, CineBrain, and SG-MIND naturalistic fMRI datasets
sample_scale: 30 participants total: Algonauts four subjects and about 260 person-hours; CineBrain six and about 36 hours; SG-MIND 20, 8,519 clips and 140.7 hours
institution_count: Multiple datasets/sites; SG-MIND is collected at one NUS site; exact aggregate institution count NI
split_strategy: Fixed-seed 80/20 held-out-stimulus split per benchmark; Algonauts season 6 is held-out external content
observation_process: Regular fMRI TR grids of 0.719, 0.80, or 1.49 seconds aligned to video, audio, and text; brain signals represented in 1,000 parcels
missingness: SG-MIND motion censoring/interpolation is described; other dataset missing-data handling NI
state: Latent ROI-level whole-brain fMRI state with subject-specific decoding
observation_decoder: Subject-specific decoder predicts whole-brain parcel responses
action: Temporally aligned video, audio, and text stimulus tokens; no treatment or control action
transition_mechanism: Causal Transformer predicts next latent with stimulus-conditioned AdaLN and SIGReg; stage 1 uses teacher forcing and stage 2 autoregressive latent rollout
maximum_horizon: Default 20 TRs; evaluated to 50 and 100 TRs; elapsed time depends on dataset TR
rollout_regime: Stage 1 teacher-forced next-state learning; stage 2 free-runs from one observed TR under a fixed stimulus stream
capability_claim: Passive stimulus-conditioned forecasting, not causal intervention or counterfactual simulation
baselines: Linear model, causally masked TRIBE, MIRAGE, and quoted BrainVista results
state_fidelity_metrics: Global correlation, mean parcel-wise Pearson correlation, and classification at Top-10
transition_metrics: Forecast correlation and classification metrics across horizons
rollout_stability: Performance reported at 20, 50, and 100 TR horizons; no physiological-constraint failure rate
action_sensitivity: Mismatched temporal stimulus alignment and modality-removal ablations
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI; no predictive calibration or uncertainty evaluation
external_validation: Three datasets and held-out Algonauts content; no unseen-subject or independent clinical-cohort validation
decision_utility: Neuroscience simulation and interpretability only; no clinical decision utility
statistical_analysis: Interpretability uses 1,000-spin tests with FDR correction; predictive comparisons lack confidence intervals and repeated-seed variance
causal_language: Causal denotes past-only attention, not causal-effect identification
estimand: Prediction of brain response to observed naturalistic stimuli
data_access: Public benchmark datasets plus SG-MIND; SG-MIND access terms NI
preprocessing_reproducibility: Alignment, parcellation, architecture, splits, and training are described
randomness: Fixed split seed reported; repeated model seeds NI
evidence_anchors: Abstract p.1; Sec. III and Fig. 3 pp.3-5; Sec. IV, Tables I-III pp.5-8; Discussion pp.9-10
appraisal_strengths: Clear teacher-forcing versus rollout stages, horizon analysis, stimulus-mismatch test, modality ablations, and three benchmarks
appraisal_limitations: Causal wording is temporal only; no uncertainty; subject-specific heads evaluate seen cohorts; SG-MIND access is unclear; no confidence intervals for forecasting

title: Open-H-Embodiment: A Large-Scale Dataset for Enabling Foundation Models in Medical Robotics
domain: Medical robotics and surgical multi-embodiment video prediction
dataset_or_cohort: Open-H-Embodiment and the C-H-S-S world-model subset
sample_scale: Open-H: 119 datasets, 780 hours, 125,815 episodes, 20 platforms, 33 task families; C-H-S-S: 32 datasets and nine embodiments
split_strategy: Each constituent dataset uses a 5% held-out test; C-H-S-S evaluates two episodes from each of 25 eligible datasets with fixed selection seed; seven datasets excluded for clips shorter than 72 frames
observation_process: Synchronized heterogeneous surgical video and robot kinematics; approximately 10-fps normalized clips; actions normalized by embodiment
state: Single context image and latent video state
observation_decoder: Generates 12 future RGB frames per chunk
action_provenance: Recorded demonstrated robot actions replayed open-loop
transition_mechanism: Two-billion-parameter Cosmos-Predict2.5 latent video diffusion Transformer with MLP action conditioning
maximum_horizon: Seventy-two frames in six 12-frame chunks, approximately 7.2 seconds at 10 fps
rollout_regime: Autoregressive free-running video chunks conditioned on replayed recorded actions; not closed-loop action selection
capability_claim: Action-conditioned, multi-embodiment surgical simulation; closed-loop policy utility is broader project motivation rather than a C-H-S-S result
baselines: Policy comparisons include GR00T-N1.6 and ACT; world-model comparisons lack a matched action-agnostic baseline
transition_metrics: Per-frame L1 and SSIM over generated horizons; separate policy task success
rollout_stability: Per-frame/chunk drift, sawtooth behavior, three-seed variability, and benchtop-versus-tissue stratification
action_sensitivity: NI; no action removal, shuffle, or perturbation test
calibration_and_uncertainty: Three generation seeds with mean and SD; no probabilistic calibration
external_validation: Broad multisite and multiplatform coverage within the assembled datasets; no independent live-tissue clinical deployment
decision_utility: In-silico evaluation and synthetic-data/policy research; no validated human-surgery decision utility
safety_evaluation: Limitations analyze failures, unexpected events, and absence of live tissue; no formal simulator-hazard evaluation
statistical_analysis: World model reports mean and SD over three seeds; policy success has Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence intervals
causal_language: No causal-effect claim; predicts physical visual consequences under recorded actions
estimand: Conditional future-video prediction under demonstrated actions
weights_access: Public model checkpoints are linked; exact license varies by component and is NI
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed schema, normalization, conversion, filtering, model, and evaluation protocol
randomness: Fixed episode-selection seed and three generation seeds
evidence_anchors: Abstract pp.1-2; Results pp.7-9 and Table 1; C-H-S-S pp.18-22 and Fig. 7; Methods pp.25-29; Data Availability p.36
appraisal_strengths: Large, diverse, open resource; actual kinematic action conditioning; horizon- and seed-stratified evaluation; confidence intervals for policy success
appraisal_limitations: Open-loop action replay and pixel metrics; success-demo bias; only two episodes per dataset; no action intervention test or broad closed-loop validation

title: SAW: Toward a Surgical Action World Model via Controllable and Scalable Video Generation
domain: Laparoscopic surgical video generation and augmentation
dataset_or_cohort: Curated clips from 21 YouTube videos plus 80 videos from HeiChole, Cholec80, SurgVU, and CRCD
sample_scale: 12,044 final clips from 101 source videos; paper separately lists 2,760 and 12,878 source clips, which does not reconcile with the final count
institution_count: Multiple public datasets and online videos; exact institution count NI
split_strategy: Source-video split: 11,502 training clips and 542 test clips
observation_process: Eighty-one-frame 25-fps RGB clips at 1024 by 576 with language, tissue affordance, and 2D tool-tip tracks
state: First RGB frame, tissue-affordance representation, language condition, and planned 2D trajectory
action: Two-dimensional tool-tip trajectory plus language action context; not a robot kinematic command
action_provenance: Extracted from observed video or user/simulator supplied at generation time
transition_mechanism: LTX latent diffusion/flow-matching model with IC-LoRA conditioning and a longitudinal depth-consistency loss
rollout_regime: Single-shot diffusion conditioned on the entire planned trajectory; no autoregressive closed-loop control
capability_claim: Controllable action-video synthesis, not planning or counterfactual clinical simulation
baselines: WAN, LTX, SurgSora; downstream CNN and ViT recognition models
state_fidelity_metrics: FVD, condition-aware CD-FVD, SSIM, PSNR, and LPIPS; downstream per-class F1
transition_metrics: Video similarity and condition-aware generation metrics
rollout_stability: CD-FVD tests condition consistency, but no long-rollout or constraint-failure evaluation
action_sensitivity: Removal of trajectory, affordance, language, first frame, or depth-consistency loss
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI; no calibration or predictive uncertainty
external_validation: Held-out source videos only; no independent clinical site
decision_utility: Rare-action augmentation and qualitative simulator rendering; no measured clinician or robot decision impact
safety_evaluation: Depth consistency targets geometry; no collision, harm, or physical-safety test
statistical_analysis: No confidence intervals or repeated-seed variance reported
estimand: Conditional surgical video generation under a supplied 2D path
data_access: Component datasets have mixed public access; curated annotations and assembled corpus availability NI
preprocessing_reproducibility: Clip construction, conditions, architecture, and training are described
evidence_anchors: Abstract p.1; Sec. 2 and Fig. 1 pp.2-4; Sec. 3 and Tables 1-2 pp.4-6; Sec. 4 and Table 3 pp.6-9; Conclusion p.10
appraisal_strengths: Source-video split, multiple conditioning ablations, condition-aware metrics, and downstream real-test augmentation
appraisal_limitations: Short open-loop videos; no kinematic actions, closed loop, clinical safety, uncertainty, or artifact release; reported source-clip arithmetic is internally inconsistent

title: Surgical WAM: A World-Action Model for Data-Efficient Surgical Robot Learning
dataset_or_cohort: SurRoL simulated dVRK tasks; prior surgical-video checkpoint; qualitative JIGSAWS extension
sample_scale: 10,000 SurRoL demonstrations across four tasks; 100 evaluation episodes per reported result; exact action-free pretraining scale NI
institution_count: Simulation plus JIGSAWS public data; institution count NA for simulation and NI for qualitative real-video source aggregation
split_strategy: Demonstration train/test split details NI; evaluations use 100 simulation episodes
observation_process: Current endoscopic RGB, robot proprioception, task text, and recurrent closed-loop observations
censoring_or_competing_events: Episode termination and failure handling are task-specific; exact censoring rules NI
state: Current image, proprioceptive state, and task instruction
observation_decoder: Jointly predicts future video/state tokens and a 16-action chunk
action: Absolute Cartesian end-effector targets and gripper command
action_provenance: Executed robot actions from demonstrations during training and model-generated actions during control
transition_mechanism: Cosmos Policy diffusion Transformer jointly models video and action sequences
maximum_horizon: Action chunk 16; default execution horizon four actions before replanning; maximum episode length NI
rollout_regime: Closed-loop receding-horizon control: predict a chunk, execute a prefix, observe, and replan
capability_claim: Closed-loop surgical robot planning and control
baselines: BET, DEX, ALOHA, Diffusion Policy, and pi0.5; matched WAM without action-free pretraining
state_fidelity_metrics: Closed-loop task-success rate; no direct generated-state fidelity metric
transition_metrics: No separate one-step transition metric; success reflects combined model and control
rollout_stability: Success compared for execution horizons 1, 2, 4, and 8 and across training checkpoints
action_sensitivity: NI; no action-shuffle, perturbation, or dose-response analogue
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI; no calibrated action or state uncertainty
external_validation: JIGSAWS provides qualitative real-video adaptation only; no quantitative real-robot closed-loop validation
safety_evaluation: No formal collision, hazard, or constraint evaluation; quantitative tests are simulation-only
statistical_analysis: One hundred episodes per result; no confidence intervals or repeated-seed variance reported
estimand: Closed-loop task success under the learned policy
data_access: SurRoL and JIGSAWS are public; adapted training artifacts and checkpoint access NI
preprocessing_reproducibility: Architecture and main training settings are described; data split, extraction, and some checkpoint details are insufficient
evidence_anchors: Abstract pp.1-2; Sec. 3 and Fig. 2 pp.4-5; Sec. 4, Tables 1-3, and Fig. 3 pp.5-8; Conclusion pp.7-8
appraisal_strengths: Direct closed-loop evaluation, matched action-free-pretraining ablation, strong policy baselines, and execution-horizon analysis
appraisal_limitations: Quantitative evidence is simulation-only; no visual-fidelity, uncertainty, formal safety, or quantitative real-data result; split, randomness, and release details are unclear

title: SWoMo: Neuro-Symbolic World Model for Cataract Surgery Simulation
sample_scale: 868 Cataract-1K videos and 50 CATARACTS videos; six surgical phases
institution_count: At least two source datasets; exact contributing institution count NI
split_strategy: Video-level 80/10/10 split for Cataract-1K and 50/6/44 split for CATARACTS
observation_process: Four-fps, 16-frame RGB clips resized to 128 by 128 with anatomy, tool, phase, and scene-graph annotations
state: Rule-based simulator anatomy and tool kinematics, scene graph, and optional initial image
action: Explicit tool-motion changes in the rule simulator
action_provenance: Extracted/replayed from observed video or generated by the simulator
transition_mechanism: Deterministic Godot rule simulator plus scene-graph-, image-, and video-conditioned diffusion with ControlNet
maximum_horizon: Sixteen frames or four seconds; full videos are chained autoregressively for augmentation
rollout_regime: Fixed-action simulation for each clip; autoregressive chaining for downstream full-video generation; no learned closed-loop policy
baselines: StyleGAN-V, Endora, MedSora, LVDM, MOFA, and SG2VID
state_fidelity_metrics: FVD, FID, LPIPS diversity, tool-detection bounding-box IoU and F1, and downstream phase accuracy/F1
rollout_stability: NI; no explicit long-rollout drift or physical-constraint failure rate
action_sensitivity: Scene-graph and image-conditioning ablations; qualitative novel-motion tests
external_validation: Evaluated on two datasets and cross-style transfer; no held-out institution or clinical outcome validation
decision_utility: Data augmentation for phase recognition; no trainee, clinician, or robot decision-impact evaluation
safety_evaluation: Rule simulator supplies physical structure, but no constraint-violation or hazard test
statistical_analysis: No confidence intervals or repeated-seed variance reported
estimand: Conditional surgical-video prediction under specified tool motion
weights_access: Public checkpoints linked; exact licenses NI
data_access: Public base datasets and project artifacts are linked; base-data access remains dataset-specific
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed simulator, graph, clip, model, and training description

domain: ICU treatment policy learning under hidden confounding
dataset_or_cohort: Synthetic sepsis environment and HiRID ICU database
sample_scale: HiRID contains more than 33,000 ICU admissions; synthetic and real experiments are repeated over 10 runs; real trajectories truncated at 20 hours
institution_count: HiRID is from Bern University Hospital; synthetic environment has no institution
split_strategy: Uses standard HiRID benchmark splits and synthetic train/evaluation samples; exact counts in the inspected text NI
observation_process: Hourly EHR states for up to 20 hours; real state has 203/204 variables plus SOFA; synthetic simulator supplies known dynamics
missingness: HiRID preprocessing follows an open benchmark, but exact missing-data handling in the primary paper NI
censoring_or_competing_events: Trajectories are truncated to 20 hours; discharge/death competing-event treatment NI
state: Observed EHR state plus a latent confounder representation across compatible worlds
observation_decoder: Predicts policy/value quantities and compatible-world distributions; it does not decode future patient observations
action: Two binary decisions: intravenous fluids and vasopressors
action_provenance: Observed clinician actions in HiRID; simulator policy in synthetic data
transition_mechanism: Variational ensemble of compatible latent-confounder worlds with behavior-policy and value models; pessimistic Bellman updates penalize delphic uncertainty
maximum_horizon: Twenty decision steps in synthetic experiments and 20 hours for HiRID
rollout_regime: Offline policy optimization and off-policy evaluation; no generative patient-state rollout

title: Cosmos-H-Surgical: Learning Surgical Robot Policies from Videos via World Modeling

institution_count: Public videos span several datasets/sources; real robot uses one anonymized commercial platform, institution count NI
